channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: US Lead in AI Over China Narrows After DeepSeek Gains, BI Says
item.description: American AI companies’ performance lead over China narrowed sharply in past months to a record low after labs such as DeepSeek gained ground, threatening US tech supremacy, according to Bloomberg Intelligence.
item.dc:creator: Saritha Rai

item.title: AI Whistleblowers, Google, OpenAI, Meta to Face New York City Council
item.description: Former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon, who warned that artificial intelligence could become too powerful for humans to control, will testify Monday at a New York City Council hearing alongside representatives of some of the world’s biggest AI companies.
item.dc:creator: Nacha Cattan and Laura Nahmias

item.title: AI Stocks Drive an Increasingly Divided Market
item.description: Schwab Head of Macro Research and Strategy Kevin Gordon tells Bloomberg This Weekend that AI-related technology stocks are supporting the broader market even as many individual companies have suffered significantly larger declines, highlighting increasingly narrow market leadership. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Gordon says a gradual Federal Reserve tightening cycle and a labor market that avoids widespread layoffs could support stocks, while investors are increasingly focused on whether companies sustain their enormous AI capital spending. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple’s John Ternus Leads Design; Touch-Screen OLED MacBook Pro Gets Lighter
item.description: Also: A big update on the touch-screen MacBook Pro.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gurman

item.title: 48 Hours in the Singapore With No Smartphone
item.description: Bloomberg Pursuits Senior Features Writer Thu-Huong Ha tells Bloomberg This Weekend about spending 48 hours in Singapore without relying on a smartphone, navigating a city where transportation, payments, dining and government services are deeply integrated with digital technology. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Ha says the experiment required more patience and effort but also made her more observant of her surroundings and convinced her there is value in experiencing boredom without immediately reaching for a screen. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Names Clayton, Ferguson to Lead AI Task Force
item.description: The “Super Intelligence Force” will be led by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton and chairman of the Federal Trade Commission Andrew Ferguson, President Donald Trump says on Truth Social.
item.dc:creator: Sam Kim

item.title: SoftBank’s Masayoshi Son Has Rare Cautionary Note on AI Safety
item.description: SoftBank Group Corp. chief Masayoshi Son — one of AI’s fervent believers — said that even he’s worried about safety risks as machines quickly gain more abilities.
item.dc:creator: Mayumi Negishi

item.title: Britain’s Reliance on US Cloud Giants Alarms Its Politicians
item.description: The UK’s dependence on big American cloud providers poses “a strategic and economic vulnerability” to the country, politicians warned, as US authorities have the power to switch off Britain’s public services or demand personal information under federal law.
item.dc:creator: Philip Aldrick and Jacob Reid

item.title: Korea Orders Security Checks After Finance-Sector Data Leaks
item.description: South Korean regulators urged financial institutions to promptly complete internal security inspections and report the results to authorities after a series of cyberattacks led to personal data breaches across the industry.
item.dc:creator: Jaehyun Eom

item.title: Trump Taps Clayton for AI Task Force in Response to Safety Fears
item.description: President Donald Trump said he appointed Jay Clayton, his director of national intelligence, to help lead a White House task force on artificial intelligence as the fast-moving technology raises concerns about its safety risks.
item.dc:creator: María Paula Mijares Torres
